correctness.rationale: Exactly computed conditional success probability for both taxa is (1-exp(-lambda S))^2. For any two positive unequal efforts, conditioning on other bottles makes split dependence a strictly convex quadratic in s=exp(-lambda x)+exp(-lambda y), so at least one endpoint strictly improves the objective and all optimizers have equal positive entries. Exact polynomial factorization proves a unique one-versus-three crossing; exact rational bounds prove k=2 strictly worse there, with continuity yielding nearby skip of two. Standalone check.py reproduces the critical identities with rational arithmetic; finite spot checks are supplementary.

value.rationale: For jointly detecting two taxa, sample-level viability is a motivated failure mechanism and joint co-detection is a natural target that cannot be reduced to maximizing expected richness. The theorem replaces a high-dimensional, nonconcave continuous effort optimization by n explicit values and exhibits an abrupt optimal replication jump from one to three that skips the intermediate sample count despite zero fixed sample costs; it identifies a substantive design boundary rather than an arbitrary finite parameter tally.
